newsitem.title: USA: Texaco's Pembroke costs down 25 mln.
newsitem.headline: Texaco's Pembroke costs down 25 mln.

text.p: Texaco Inc has reduced the costs at its Pembroke refinery in Britain by 25 million in the past year, Vice President Clarence P Cazalot Jr said Wednesday.
He told analysts this lowered the refinery's breakeven cost to $1.85 a barrel from $2.30.
He said Texaco's agreement to buy Gulf's 35 percent interest in Pembroke cracking company would lead to further earnings increases through improved operating flexibility.
He said the purchase will also lead to closure of Gulf's 115,000 barrel per day refinery at Milford Haven in mid-1997, reducing the availability of clean product in the area by 25 percent.
Cazalot said front-end enginering work on the Nerefco consolidation has been approved and Texaco's share of the cost is $65 million.
The consolidation of facilities in The Netherlands will lead to ending operations at Pernis and consolidating them at Europort.
He said the consolidation has been accelerated by phasing in the project starting next year, instead of waiting for completion in 1998.
